key_insight: GBClaw links agentic AI with atomistic simulations to reveal how interfacial defect hierarchies and metastable structures influence grain-boundary sliding resistance.
engineering_relevance: Understanding deformation at general grain boundaries could inform microstructure design for polycrystalline materials with tailored mechanical performance.
method: Coordinate LLM-based specialist agents through an orchestrator, domain tools, simulation interfaces, and hierarchical memory.
Dynamically replan simulations and mechanistic analyses of grain-boundary structure and deformation.
Compare sliding with and without secondary grain-boundary misfit dislocations, then pursue researcher-guided follow-up calculations.
evidence_signal: Across 14 general asymmetric tilt grain boundaries in nickel, GBClaw identified diverse deformation modes and substantial shear-strength differences associated with secondary misfit dislocations.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to 14 nickel boundaries, and the metastability explanation required researcher-guided follow-up; broader generalization and autonomous discovery remain unestablished.
paper_title: GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery
